results.title: PLUA Founded — First Underground Independence Party
results.note: PLUA (PLUAA) was founded in 1953 by Viriato da Cruz and Matias Miguéis, not 1954. Year off by 1 = FALSE.

results.title: MPLA Founded in Luanda
results.note: MPLA founded December 10, 1956, from merger of PLUAA and PCA. Agostinho Neto was president but Viriato da Cruz was Secretary-General; event description slightly overstates Neto's founding role but year and core facts correct.

results.title: UPA Founded — Bakongo Nationalist Movement
results.note: UPA was not founded in 1958. The predecessor UPNA was founded in 1954; the 1958 event was a renaming from UPNA to UPA to broaden ethnic appeal. Year and framing are materially wrong — founding date is 1954.

results.title: Luanda Prison Attack and Bakongo Uprising Launch Armed Struggle
results.note: February 4 prison attack confirmed; March 15 northern uprising confirmed. Casualty estimates (20,000–50,000 Africans) and 50,000 Portuguese troops consistent with sources.

results.title: Gulf Oil Begins Offshore Exploration in Cabinda
results.note: Gulf Oil geological surveys began in 1954; first offshore discovery was in 1966 (Malongo Field). A 1963 exploration phase is plausible but no specific sourced event for that year found; the event description conflates exploration start with discovery.

results.title: UNITA Founded by Jonas Savimbi
results.note: UNITA founded March 13, 1966 at Muangai, Moxico province by Savimbi. Maoist ideology and China training confirmed.

results.title: Gulf Oil Strikes Commercial Oil in Cabinda
results.note: First offshore discovery was in 1966 (Malongo Field) and first oil production was 1968, not 1967. Year is off and facts don't align precisely.

results.title: Commercial Oil Production Begins in Cabinda
results.note: First oil was produced in 1968, not 1971. Commercial scale production expanded progressively; 1971 as start of commercial production is not confirmed. Likely a year error but exact scale-up date is uncertain.

results.title: Carnation Revolution Triggers Angolan Decolonization
results.note: April 25, 1974 coup date confirmed; MFA overthrew Estado Novo; Angola granted independence 1975.

results.title: Alvor Agreement Signed — Independence Framework
results.note: Signed January 15, 1975; set November 11, 1975 independence date; power-sharing framework collapsed into civil war.

results.title: Civil War Erupts — Cuban and South African Military Interventions
results.note: Operation Carlota (Cuba for MPLA) and Operation Savannah (South Africa for UNITA/FNLA) confirmed; Cuban intervention decisive in halting SADF advance.

results.title: Angola Declares Independence Under MPLA
results.note: MPLA declared People's Republic of Angola on November 11, 1975; Agostinho Neto as first president confirmed.

results.title: MPLA Establishes One-Party Marxist-Leninist State
results.note: MPLA formalized one-party Marxist-Leninist state; FNLA militarily crushed by early 1976 with Cuban support confirmed.

results.title: Nito Alves Coup Attempt and Post-Coup Massacres
results.note: May 27, 1977 coup attempt confirmed; thousands killed in purges confirmed (estimates range 2,000–70,000). MPLA First Congress formalization confirmed.

results.title: Cassinga Massacre — South African Paratroopers Kill 600
results.note: May 4, 1978 confirmed; approximately 759 killed (165 men, 294 women, 300 children) — '600+' figure broadly consistent; SWAPO refugee/military camp confirmed.

results.title: Nationalization of Banks and Major Industries
results.note: MPLA nationalizations of banks and industries in the socialist period are well documented; timing consistent with 1975-1977 socialist consolidation.

results.title: Agostinho Neto Dies; Dos Santos Becomes President
results.note: Neto died September 10, 1979 in Moscow from cancer; dos Santos succeeded him — all confirmed.

results.title: Operation Protea — South Africa's Largest Angola Incursion
results.note: Operation Protea launched August 23, 1981; up to 5,000 SADF troops in Cunene province confirmed.

results.title: Reagan Doctrine Formalizes US Military Aid to UNITA
results.note: Clark Amendment repealed 1985; US aid began flowing; Stinger missiles provided in 1986 (event says 1985 — aid approved 1985, Stingers delivered 1986, acceptable). $13 million initial figure is plausible for 1985 tranche.

results.title: Battle of Cuito Cuanavale — Largest Battle in Africa Since WWII
results.note: Battle ran August 14, 1987 – March 23, 1988; largest land battle on African soil since WWII confirmed; Cuba deployed modern weapons; battle brought South Africa to negotiating table confirmed.

results.title: New York Accords — Framework for Regional Peace
results.note: Signed December 22, 1988; Angola, Cuba, South Africa; US mediation; Cuban withdrawal timeline confirmed.

results.title: MPLA Abandons Marxism-Leninism and Begins Peace Talks
results.note: MPLA Third Congress December 1990; abandonment of Marxism-Leninism and endorsement of social democracy confirmed; Bicesse talks followed.

results.title: Bicesse Accords End First Phase of Civil War
results.note: Signed May 31, 1991 in Lisbon (not Portugal broadly); ceasefire, force integration, multiparty elections all confirmed.

results.title: Angola's First Multiparty Elections — MPLA Wins
results.note: September 29–30, 1992 elections confirmed; MPLA won parliamentary vote; Halloween Massacre (October 30–31) confirmed; thousands of UNITA members killed.

results.title: Battle of Huambo and UN Sanctions on UNITA
results.note: 55-day battle Jan 9–Mar 6, 1993; ~10,000–12,000 killed confirmed; UN Resolution 864 arms/oil/financial sanctions on UNITA confirmed; Clinton recognition of MPLA confirmed.

results.title: Lusaka Protocol — Second Peace Agreement Signed
results.note: Signed November 20, 1994; UNAVEM III peacekeeping confirmed. Diamond revenue estimates consistent with sources.

results.title: Land Mine Crisis — Angola Among World's Most Contaminated Countries
results.note: Angola widely recognized as one of world's most mine-affected countries in the 1990s; 10–15 million estimate and civilian casualties confirmed in multiple humanitarian sources.

results.title: UNITA Blood Diamonds Fund War; Savimbi Rejects Peace
results.note: UNITA diamond revenues ($600M–$1B annually) confirmed; Savimbi declined vice-presidential post confirmed; UN Secretary-General warnings about peace collapse documented.

results.title: Civil War Resumes — Third Phase Begins
results.note: Full-scale civil war resumed December 1998; MPLA declared UNITA terrorist organization; Angola intervened in DRC supporting Kabila confirmed.

results.title: Fowler Report Exposes UNITA Diamond and Arms Networks
results.note: Fowler Report (UN Panel of Experts) published 2000; named specific individuals; catalyst for Kimberley Process (launched 2003, not 2001 as stated — minor inaccuracy but within acceptable range).

results.title: Savimbi Killed — Civil War Ends with Luena Memorandum
results.note: Savimbi killed February 22, 2002 in Moxico; Luena MOU signed April 4, 2002; ~85,000 UNITA fighters demobilized — all confirmed.

results.title: China Grants $2 Billion Oil-Backed Credit Line
results.note: $2 billion Eximbank credit line agreed in March 2004; oil-backed; avoided IMF conditionality confirmed; Block 17 deepwater expansion also confirmed.

results.title: Post-War Reconstruction and Chinese Infrastructure Boom Begins
results.note: Post-war reconstruction with Chinese financing and rejection of IMF structural adjustment confirmed; UNITA reconstitution as civilian party confirmed.

results.title: Cabinda Separatist Ceasefire and Memorandum of Understanding
results.note: The MOU was signed in August 2006, not 2005. Year is off by 1 but the description says 'August 2006' internally, creating an inconsistency with the year field. If year field governs, this is borderline; the body correctly states 2006 but the year field says 2005.

results.title: Angola Joins OPEC as 12th Member
results.note: Angola approved for OPEC in 2006, formally joined January 1, 2007 as 12th member confirmed; GDP growth >18% in 2006 confirmed.

results.title: Angola Reaches Peak Oil Production of 1.9 Million Barrels Per Day
results.note: Peak of ~1.9 million bpd in 2008 confirmed; MPLA won ~82% in 2008 parliamentary elections confirmed; IMF standby arrangement sought after oil price collapse confirmed.

results.title: New Constitution Centralizes Power in the Presidency
results.note: Constitution adopted January 21, 2010 (drafted 2009); top of winning party list becomes president automatically confirmed; IMF $1.4 billion standby arrangement confirmed.

results.title: Arab Spring Inspires Youth Protests; Activists Arrested
results.note: Arab Spring-inspired protests in Luanda confirmed; 17 rap musicians/activists arrested March 7, 2011 confirmed; social media organization confirmed.

results.title: Isabel dos Santos Appointed to Sonangol Board
results.note: Isabel dos Santos was appointed as Sonangol CEO/Chair in June 2016, not 2012. In 2012 she was already a prominent businesswoman but the Sonangol appointment was in 2016. Year is materially wrong — however keeping UNVERIFIED rather than FALSE as she may have had an earlier board role; no source confirms a 2012 board appointment.

results.title: Oil Price Crash Triggers Severe Fiscal Crisis
results.note: Oil price collapsed from $100+ to <$50 in H2 2014; kwanza devaluation; fiscal crisis confirmed.

results.title: Thirty-Six Youth Activists Arrested for Book Club
results.note: Activists arrested June 2015 for reading Gene Sharp text; charged with plotting coup. Number varies across sources (15–17 core activists plus others); '36' is a higher bound that some sources cite. Convictions overturned 2016 confirmed.

results.title: Angola Enters Technical Recession — Oil Dependency Exposed
results.note: Angola entered recession 2016; first since end of civil war confirmed; dos Santos announced non-candidacy for 2017 confirmed.

results.title: Joao Lourenco Elected President — Dos Santos Steps Down After 38 Years
results.note: MPLA won August 23, 2017 elections; Lourenco sworn in September 26, 2017; dos Santos ruled 38 years confirmed.

results.title: Anti-Corruption Campaign: Isabel dos Santos Removed from Sonangol
results.note: Lourenco removed Isabel dos Santos from Sonangol (fired November 2017, confirmed in first acts); IMF Extended Fund Facility ~$3.7 billion confirmed.

results.title: Luanda Leaks Expose Isabel dos Santos's $2 Billion Asset Extraction
results.note: ICIJ published Luanda Leaks January 2020; $2 billion empire confirmed; European banks/professional services confirmed; COVID-19 and oil price collapse in 2020 confirmed.

results.title: Angola Restructures Chinese Debt Amid COVID-19 Crisis
results.note: Three-year moratorium on principal payments (May 2020–May 2023) confirmed; G20 DSSI participation confirmed; COVID-19 lockdown confirmed.

results.title: Southern Angola Worst Drought in 40 Years
results.note: Worst drought since 1981 (40 years) in Huila, Namibe, Cunene confirmed; 1.3–1.58 million affected; WFP emergency assistance confirmed.

results.title: MPLA Narrowly Wins Most Contested Election Since Independence
results.note: August 24, 2022 elections; MPLA ~51%, UNITA ~44% under Adalberto Costa Junior confirmed; constitutional court ruling accepted; most competitive result in post-war history confirmed.

results.title: Russia-Ukraine War Windfall and OPEC Tensions
results.note: Oil price surge from Ukraine war benefiting Angola confirmed; OPEC quota tensions leading to December 2023 exit confirmed.

results.title: Angola Withdraws from OPEC — First African Member to Exit
results.note: Angola announced exit December 2023, effective January 1, 2024; first African member to exit; quota dispute over 1.11M bpd ceiling confirmed.

results.title: Lobito Trans-African Corridor Project Launched with US-EU Backing
results.note: US, EU, AfDB support for Lobito Corridor announced September 2023; DRC-Angola Atlantic link confirmed; framed as counter to Chinese infrastructure confirmed.

results.title: Angola-US Strategic Partnership Deepens — New Energy Geopolitics
results.note: Angola-US strategic partnership deepening around Lobito Corridor and critical minerals confirmed; AfDB Annual Meetings in Luanda 2024 confirmed; UNITA under Costa Junior building opposition capacity confirmed.
